paper_title: The challenge with high permittivity acceptors in organic solar cells: a case study with Y-series derivatives

knowledge_points.content: A new synthetic route for Y-series acceptors uses 3-bromothiophene and elemental sulfur to create a functionalized thienothiophene (TT) building block, allowing for easier side-chain modification at the outer thiophene position compared to the traditional Friedel-Crafts acylation route.
knowledge_points.evidence: In the first step, 3-bromothiophene is activated by a metal-halogen exchange reaction with n-BuLi... followed by quenching with elemental sulfur... Overall, this short synthesis route enables both, a later functionalization of the universal precursor (4), and a wider range of usable side chains.

knowledge_points.content: The relative permittivity (εr) of Y-series acceptors is significantly increased by the introduction of triethylene glycol (TEG) side chains, reaching 4.73 for Y-thio-EG and 5.24 for Y-pyr-EG, compared to 2.39 for the standard Y6 acceptor at 1 kHz.
knowledge_points.evidence: Exemplary at 1 kHz (Table 1), εr of Y-thio-EG and Y-pyr-EG increased by approx. 100% from 2.39 (for Y6) to 4.73 and 5.24, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: Binary organic solar cells using PM6 as the donor and the glycol-modified acceptors achieved power conversion efficiencies (PCE) of 8.19% for Y-thio-EG and 5.26% for Y-pyr-EG, which are lower than typical Y6-based devices.
knowledge_points.evidence: OSCs with Y-thio-EG and Y-pyr-EG merely achieved a PCE of 8.19% (FF 58.7%) and 5.26% (FF 40.3%), respectively.

knowledge_points.content: The introduction of polar triethylene glycol (TEG) side chains increases the surface free energy (SFE) of Y-series acceptors from 41 mN/m (Y6) to 61 mN/m (Y-thio-EG) and 56 mN/m (Y-pyr-EG), primarily due to an increase in the polar component.
knowledge_points.evidence: Compared to Y6 (SFE 41 ± 6 mN m−1), Y-thio-EG and Y-pyr-EG exhibit increased SFE values of 61 ± 3 mN m−1 and 56 ± 2 mN m−1, respectively. The increase stems from a new, polar contribution of the TEG chains to the SFE.

knowledge_points.content: The lack of side-chain branching points in Y-pyr-EG leads to tighter molecular packing and higher crystallinity compared to Y-thio-EG, resulting in a higher relative permittivity (5.24 vs 4.73) and a shorter π-π stacking distance (0.34 nm vs 0.36 nm).
knowledge_points.evidence: The difference between Y-thio-EG and Y-pyr-EG most likely indicates tighter molecular packing of Y-pyr-EG due to the lack of the central side chain branching points... The pristine Y-pyr-EG sample exhibits a π–π stacking distance of 0.34 nm... which is significantly lower than the one of Y-thio-EG with 0.36 nm.

knowledge_points.content: High ideality factors (n) of 2.82 for PM6:Y-thio-EG and 2.08 for PM6:Y-pyr-EG suggest significant energetic disorder in the active layer, likely caused by the electrostatic disorder from randomly distributed glycol dipoles.
knowledge_points.evidence: the OSCs based on Y-thio-EG and Y-pyr-EG exhibit an ideality factor of 2.82 and 2.08, respectively... According to Xiong et al., the deviation to higher values indicates a large energetic disorder in the active layer.

knowledge_points.content: The Flory–Huggins interaction parameter (χ) between the donor PM6 and the glycol-modified acceptors is significantly higher (7.9–9.9) than with Y6 (2.9), indicating a lower miscibility that challenges the formation of an optimal bulk heterojunction morphology.
knowledge_points.evidence: the Flory–Huggins interaction parameters χ for both acceptors with common donor polymers (Table 3). The values are generally high in the range of 7 to 9, compared to more typical values as seen for Y6 (in the range of 2 to 3).

knowledge_points.content: STEM-EELS elemental mapping of sulfur and nitrogen is used to visualize donor and acceptor phases in PM6:Y-series blends, utilizing the higher sulfur weight percentage in PM6 (21 wt%) compared to the acceptors (9-10 wt%).
knowledge_points.evidence: The donor PM6 contains 21 wt% sulfur (in the repeating unit), while both acceptors only contain 9–10 wt% sulfur. This difference leads to a usable contrast between donor and acceptor phase in the STEM-EELS elemental mapping images.

knowledge_points.content: The substitution of alkyl chains with triethylene glycol (TEG) side chains in Y-series acceptors slightly reduces thermal stability, with decomposition temperatures (5% weight loss) of 330°C for Y-thio-EG and 287°C for Y-pyr-EG.
knowledge_points.evidence: Y-thio-EG and Y-pyr-EG exhibit decomposition temperatures ([5% weight loss) of 330 °C and 287 °C, respectively... shows that the TEG chains slightly decrease the thermal stability.

knowledge_points.content: While Y-thio-EG exhibits a high exciton dissociation efficiency (ηdiss) of 97.3%, its charge collection efficiency (ηcc) is limited to 87.4%, and Y-pyr-EG shows even lower efficiencies (ηdiss 83.4%, ηcc 60.5%), indicating that charge transport and collection are major bottlenecks.
knowledge_points.evidence: Both acceptors Y-thio-EG and Y-pyr-EG exhibit good to moderate values for ηdiss (97.3% and 83.4%), but poor values for ηcc (87.4% and 60.5%). This shows, that the biggest limitation can be attributed to the diffusion and collection of the free charge carriers.

knowledge_points.content: GIWAXS analysis of Y-pyr-EG reveals a high crystalline coherence length (CCL) of 29 nm for lamellar stacking (peak at qz ~ 2.1 nm⁻¹), which decreases to 20 nm when blended with PM6.
knowledge_points.evidence: The most prominent lamellar stacking peak of Y-pyr-EG located at qz 2.1 nm−1 reveals a lamellar stacking distance of 3.0 nm and a large CCL of 29 nm... In the PM6:Y-pyr-EG sample, the CCL of 20 nm... is slightly smaller compared to the pristine film (29 nm).

knowledge_points.content: The decrease in relative permittivity (εr) observed in the MHz frequency regime for glycolated Y-series acceptors indicates that the dipolar contribution from OEG chains may not be effective for ultrafast processes like exciton dissociation.
knowledge_points.evidence: the starting decrease in the MHz regime could indicate that the dipolar contribution from the OEG chains to the relative permittivity might not be effective for faster processes in the OSCs, such as the exciton dissociation.
